questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country. I chose the US to explore a destination far away from home and I was also motivated by the great universities in the US. University of California is one of these great universities and going to Berkeley which is a world renown institution was a dream of mine.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The guidance i got from University of Copenhagen was very helpful. They helped me through the UC and visa application process. The biggest challenge that I had to solve myself was housing in Berkeley which is very expensive and hard to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was in an orientation program through the UCEAP reciprocity program which helped me settle in at the university. Also the international dorm where I lived helped me settle down in Berkeley.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Fortunately, I got accepted into the international dorm called International House which is located right next to campus. I recommend anyone going to Berkeley to apply to this housing opportunity. It was expensive but the community was worth it! Apply as fast as you can!! Maybe even before you get accepted into the Berkeley campus to be safe.

I didn't look into much other off campus housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living in an off campus dorm works great. I can't say what it's like to live far away from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is haard to get housing in Berkeley. I think I was lucky. On the other hand 4 / 6 students from the University of Copenhagen got into International House so maybe you have ok odds. The two others struggled to find something nice in time for the start of the semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to apply through the UC system and try to get into your desired campus. This is a pretty long process and you don't get a reply on your application before april / may which is pretty late.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My advisor from the University of Copenhagen was a great help. I didn't communicate much with the UC personel.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I wanted. But I didn't try to apply for any grad classes or research courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do everything one step at a time. And try to write a good application in the UC platform. I think it really makes a difference in terms of campus placement.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was comparable to the University of Copenhagen. But the amount of time spent on homework was significantly higher. I think you can choose both easy and hard courses. Just check rate my professor and Berkeleytime (student run website) before signing up for anything.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More responsibility to the individual. At home I am used to having both lectures and class teachings run by a GSI. Berkeley only has lectures, short discussions and office hours. In reality, you only have to go to lectures and the rest can be done by yourself.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHY 188 - Bayesian Data Analysis and Machine Learning
DATA C88C - Computational Structures in Data Science
CHEM 135 - Chemical Biology
CHEM C150 - Introduction to Materials Chemistry

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: These courses fit me great as a nanoscience student. I would recommend all courses if there are within your field. Maybe except the physics course that had a really bad lecturer.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The housing was very expensive. More than I expected. Also you have to get health insurance which is expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than expected but also included food. General living costs in Berkeley may have been a bit cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My international dorm hosted many cultural exchange activities and other social activities like dance classes and trips to San Francisco.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to International House and participate in some of their Diversiteas. Each Wednesday a new country is hosting the event and it is super fun. Also there are alot of great sports opportunities on campus which I never really explored.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to SF. Rent a car and go se California. Lake Tahoe. Yosemite. LA. Monterey and Santa Cruz. There is so much to see!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. My english is good and americans are super friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with people from my international dorm which was a mix of international and local students. Go to bars in Berkeley and participate in events on campus. People are very friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Americans are so friendly and easy to talk to. You meet a lot of people because people are so good at socializing. I was also invited to Thanksgiving which was a super nice experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Sign up for housing in good time. Apply for International House. Apply for scholarships. It's expensive! And I was lucky to get a lot of funding partly, I think, due to the Berkeley brand.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Berkeley is a great university and I can warmly recommend going there!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends I meet at my international dorm. Getting the experience of being at one of the top universities in the world. The atmosphere is great.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Applying for everything before going.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
